- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3), model often overcorrects upward; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- After a recent spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and history shows mean reversion, forecast should be anchored to 30-day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 30-day high, flag for downward correction — especially if sentiment is flat or negative.
- For horizon >10 days, model tends to overproject upward momentum; apply a 10–15% downward bias if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment reversal” penalty: subtract 2–5% from forecast if sentiment drops below -0.2 within 3 days.
